explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/418: are there infinitely many positive integers not of the form n - φ(n)? Yes, by Browkin–Schinzel (2^k·509203, k ≥ 1). The statement asserts that the complement of {n - φ n} in ℕ is infinite. Including 0 makes no difference, since 0 = 0 - φ(0) is in the range anyway. Faithful.
